artifact.path: repository root and checked-in proof/skill evidence
artifact.working_tree: dirty because this release record and status updates are part of the reviewed change

decision_question: Is ReFolDec ready, within its stated scope, to be treated as a usable, safe, and evidence-supported recursive fold/unfold framework, and what may be released now versus what must defer for evidence?
acceptance_criteria: Classify claims as confirmed, inferred, proposal, or unknown.
Separate analytical, live, historical, and not-run evidence.
State approved, approved-with-limits, deferred, and rejected boundaries.
Keep placeholder links, runtime limits, and firewall limitations explicit.
Give blocked claims an owner, decisive next test, and consequence.
Define review expiry and earlier reopening triggers.

shared_model_or_source_limits: Review perspectives rely substantially on the same local repository sources.
The model family is not independently known.
No external organ, renderer, Agent Skills client, protected holdout, or domain-specialist adjudication was available.

evidence_checks.evidence: FOLD-CONTRACT.md 1.0.0, fixture schema 1.1, legal fold matrix, invariant rules, and deferred direct folds.
Dependency-free registry validator and tests; applies to registry integrity only.
Neutral fixture/matrix and tests cover preservation, loss, ambiguity, missing metadata, and deferred-fold rejection; no runtime.
One synthetic source with four forms, inverse artifacts, hashes, and invariant comparison.
40 packages, 36 project-owned evaluation designs ready, current task quality not-run, one historical benchmark.
Case study is representative; proof package uses synthetic public-safe source provenance.
Firewall policy and registry-specific automation exist; whole-tree clearance and external-link review were not run.
Downstream pointers remain placeholders and no owner-authorized parity reports are available.

live_checks.result: four forms, six nodes, six edges, and two flows

initial_reviews.finding: Specification and structural evidence is present; operational fold, organ, and skill outcome evidence is absent.
The repository is useful as a head-canon and contribution reference; the case study is not empirical proof.
Firewall policy is not whole-tree clearance; placeholders and client portability remain unverified.

falsification_hypotheses.claim_challenged: A fixture validator proves general fold losslessness.
falsification_hypotheses.test_that_could_prove_objection_wrong: Run an implementation-backed fold/inverse cycle on unseen fixtures.

falsification_hypotheses.claim_challenged: The representative case study proves an executed loop.
falsification_hypotheses.test_that_could_prove_objection_wrong: Archive a frozen executed fixture with source, intermediates, inverse outputs, hashes, and comparison.

falsification_hypotheses.claim_challenged: Structural skill evidence proves portability or uplift.
falsification_hypotheses.test_that_could_prove_objection_wrong: Run matched current-version evaluations with separated grading and a protected unseen holdout.

falsification_hypotheses.claim_challenged: The firewall policy proves whole-tree publication safety.
falsification_hypotheses.test_that_could_prove_objection_wrong: Perform an owner-authorized whole-tree scan and manual checklist review.

decisive_evidence: The contracts and conformance design define a coherent specification boundary.
The registry has narrow live validator/test evidence.
One synthetic proof package supports only a bounded manual analytical demonstration.
The current skill inventory explicitly limits task-quality evidence to not-run.
Organ pointers are explicitly placeholders and no parity reports are available.
negotiator.rationale: The repository supports controlled public specification and bounded fixture proof, but not runtime, broad losslessness, skill outcome, external conformance, or whole-tree publication claims.
unresolved_items: Normative mapping between explanatory core-loop stages and canonical forms.
Owner-authorized organ pointer and parity checks.

approved: Public specification/head-canon vocabulary and contract artifacts.
One bounded public-safe synthetic proof package.
Contributions through the existing issue and pull-request path within scope.
approved_with_limits: Organ links as routing context only while marked placeholders.
deferred: General runtime, operational losslessness, and generalized round trips.
Skill portability, uplift, production readiness, and task-quality claims.
External organ conformance and URL verification.
rejected: Treating validators as ecosystem-wide conformance proof.
Treating the case study as an executed event record.
Unilateral implementation of a deferred direct fold.
Starting runtime work before contract, proof, and owner-conformance gates.

follow_up.item: Publish the normative core-loop stage/transition mapping.
follow_up.next_test: Check the mapping against one fixture.
follow_up.consequence_if_false: Keep the single formal-loop claim deferred.

follow_up.item: Add a second unseen proof fixture.
follow_up.next_test: Repeat source/intermediate/inverse artifact and invariant comparison.

follow_up.item: Run current-version skill evaluations with an unseen holdout.
follow_up.next_test: Use matched isolated runs with separated or blinded grading.

follow_up.item: Confirm organ pointers and obtain parity records.
follow_up.next_test: Record all required contract, fixture, registry, firewall, fold, result, and date fields.

follow_up.item: Perform whole-tree firewall review before broad publication claims.
follow_up.next_test: Owner-authorized scan plus manual checklist and link review.

reopen_earlier_if: Contract, representation, legal/deferred fold, registry, or firewall policy changes.
A runtime surface or second proof fixture is introduced.
A downstream organ is declared conforming or a placeholder becomes a public dependency.
Skill evaluation design, package versions, or benchmark evidence changes.
A whole-tree publication review, protected benchmark, renderer run, or Agent Skills client run becomes available.
New external links, provenance claims, or sensitive-content risk enters the release surface.
